thread.title: Here's Why China Could Be an Overhang for Apple

title: Here's Why China Could Be an Overhang for Apple
text:
Here’s Why China Could Be an Overhang for Apple By Oct. 18, 2018 1:26 p.m. ET Order Reprints A cracked iPhone. Age Barros Text size
China could present some short-term issues for Apple investors—but it shouldn’t worry them too much, according to new research.
China is a crucial market for Apple’s (ticker: AAPL) business. In the quarter ended June 30 , for example, it accounted for nearly 18% of sales and 27% of operating income. And recent economic and regulatory issues there, Morgan Stanley ’s Katy Huberty wrote Wednesday, could hit the company’s services business with China, the most important market for the App Store.
“We see China as the biggest near-term risk” to the stock, Huberty wrote.
Chinese regulators have lately slowed down approvals of new games, according to reports . That hasn’t led to widespread concern that companies won’t be allowed to market games there, but it has reportedly led to quarter-to-quarter bumpiness in sales as games have moved through the process more slowly than expected. (China is the world’s biggest gaming market by several billion dollars, NewZoo said this summer .)
Meanwhile, U.S.-China trade tensions continue to concern investors, along with questions about the prospects for economic growth there. ( Read Barron’s latest market update for the effects of those issues, among others, on markets in real time.) Reports about the possible Chinese hacking of motherboards —which major tech companies, including Apple , have denied—haven’t helped. Newsletter Sign-up
This isn’t a time to panic, according to Huberty, who has an Outperform rating and a $247 price target on Apple’s stock, about 13% above current levels. She reiterated her position Wednesday even as she said thhat services revenue in the September quarter could come in below her estimates. (The shares were down nearly 3% to about $218 in early Thursday trading.)
China, she wrote, presents “a near-term overhang, but we see limited downside to near-term estimates and remain bullish on the long term sustainability of services growth.” On the hardware front, meanwhile, Emily Bary recently covered the notion that Apple’s latest phones might perform well in China , which should generally boost the services business.
“As we approach 2019, the new gaming license approval situation in China remains the most important App Store-related storyline to follow,” Huberty wrote. “Nevertheless we believe this issue will be temporary given the importance of the gaming market in China but also expect smaller/faster growing countries to continue increasing in importance, providing the end-market diversification needed to sustain App Store growth over a multiyear period.”
